krise.lira_vertrauen.name: Confidence in the lira shaken
krise.lira_vertrauen.grund: Markets do not trust the lira: {fall, select, beide {it has lost {abwertung, number, 1} % in twelve months and the risk premium stands at {cds} points} abwertung {it has lost {abwertung, number, 1} % in twelve months} cds {the risk premium stands at {cds} points} other {the thresholds are only just undercut}}. They read new spending programmes as an inflation risk.
krise.lira_vertrauen.wirkung: Spending on the economy and the budget costs {faktor, number, 1} times the usual capital.
krise.lira_vertrauen.bedingung: Ends when twelve-month depreciation falls below {abwertung} % and the risk premium below {cds} points.
krise.lira_vertrauen.ausweg: Way out: first win back confidence (leave the central bank alone, put the budget in order) or use revenue instead of spending.
krise.katastrophenlage.name: State of disaster
krise.katastrophenlage.grund: After the disaster, administration, budget and attention are focused on emergency relief and care for those affected.
krise.katastrophenlage.wirkung: Only provision (housing, health, security, infrastructure) works as before; everything else costs {faktor, number, 1} times as much, prestige projects (culture) wait.
krise.katastrophenlage.bedingung: Ends when the disaster lies more than {tage} days back and no event is open any more.
krise.katastrophenlage.ausweg: Way out: whatever serves provision (housing, health, security, infrastructure) goes ahead at once; the rest waits until the situation is over.
krise.kriegsgefahr.name: Danger of war
krise.kriegsgefahr.grund: The conflict with {land} stands at {wert} of 100; the country expects unity, not showcase projects.
krise.kriegsgefahr.wirkung: Foreign and military policy costs only {rabatt} % of the capital; prestige projects (culture) are blocked.
krise.kriegsgefahr.bedingung: Ends when no conflict with a neighbour stands above {schwelle} any more.
krise.kriegsgefahr.ausweg: Way out: defuse the conflict (talks at the negotiating table in the World view) – or wait until the tension eases.
krise.zahlungsbilanz.name: Balance-of-payments crisis
krise.zahlungsbilanz.grund: The central bank's net reserves stand at {reserven, number, 1} bn dollars: the country can barely pay for imports and debt, and the markets know it.
krise.zahlungsbilanz.wirkung: Spending on the economy and the budget costs {faktor, number, 1} times the usual capital; prestige projects (culture) are blocked. Capital flees faster (foreign exchange position).
krise.zahlungsbilanz.bedingung: Ends when net reserves are back above {schwelle} bn dollars.
krise.zahlungsbilanz.ausweg: Way out: spare the reserves (no interventions), attract capital (interest rates, market confidence, a favourable current account) – or accept the IMF programme while it is on offer.
krise.justiz_umbau.name: Judiciary under reconstruction
krise.justiz_umbau.grund: The judicial reform is being implemented; courts, ministry and judicial council are fully occupied with the overhaul.
krise.justiz_umbau.wirkung: Further judicial measures (law and justice) are blocked until the reform is complete.
krise.justiz_umbau.bedingung: Ends when the judicial reform is implemented or its law withdrawn.
krise.justiz_umbau.ausweg: Way out: complete the reform under way (or withdraw its law in parliament); then the path is clear.
ereignis.chronik.ausgesessen: Sat out – the matter never reached the desk: {ausgang}
ereignis.chronik.gaert: It keeps fermenting in the background; the matter returns more urgently (escalation {stufe} of {max}).
ereignis.log.gaert_warum: The matter was not urgent enough this month; the situation is getting worse.
